claims.claim: The RollingSync failure in which the rollout reports complete while child Applications are OutOfSync is unobservable in production: the only signal named is ApplicationSet status.applicationStatus, which is exactly the field that reports Healthy while the child is OutOfSync, and the reporter's controller logs were at warn level so no progressive-sync transition lines were emitted at all. The four measurements requested for progressive sync are time-to-trigger, time-to-complete-step-X, count of Application refreshes caused by the ApplicationSet, and which Application a sync is waiting on — none of them would move when a step is promoted to Healthy without a sync operation being created, so even after the requested metrics land this failure mode still has no number attached to it.

The confirmed behavior that each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave has no controller-level check or alert, so the interim rule that hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there is a debounce is enforced only by whoever remembers it. The one requested counter that would register the mechanism is the progressive-sync metric for how many Application refreshes were caused by the ApplicationSet, and it is still an open proposal, so today a repo that violates the restriction produces no distinguishable number.

The same serverSideDiff 'is forbidden ... cannot patch' error string is the only production signal for two different diff paths — argocd-server running the dry-run for the CLI diff in-cluster, and the application-controller reconcile path on external clusters — so the observable does not discriminate which component or which identity produced it. That is why the CI reporter, whose failing jobs are all in projects that recently enabled the sync impersonation flag, concludes the broad cluster Secret credential should have sufficed: nothing in the error output names the identity actually used for the dry-run apply.

The decision that impersonation goes behind a per-project flag and that nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed states an exit condition with no measurement behind it: no counter of projects with application.sync.impersonation.enabled set, and no diff-failure rate, is recorded anywhere. The only measured before/after in the corpus is on the opposite path — ServerSideDiff=false across roughly twenty monitoring charts producing zero cosmetic OutOfSync and requiring no ignoreDifferences — so the workaround has a baseline while the rollout gate it is meant to unblock does not.

The Reverse deletionOrder introduces an unbounded wait — it waits for one application to be fully deleted before moving onto the next — and nothing in the proposal specifies a timeout, an error signal, or an emitted metric for a wait that never completes. The requested progressive-sync measurements cover time to complete step X of the sync, meaning rollingSync steps, not deletion steps, so a Reverse teardown stalled on an Application stuck deleting would move no requested number either; the operator's only evidence is watching statuses in the UI.

The freshness signal that would detect syncing stale hydrated files already exists and is simply unconsumed: the hydrator writes a hydrator.metadata file carrying drySHA, commitTime and the reproduction commands alongside each manifest.yaml, and the proposed fix for the push-to-stage staleness bug is precisely an app annotation timestamp compared against that hydrator.metadata. Today nothing compares them, so an auto-sync that deploys whatever the stage branch last held before the external promoter moved fresh manifests is unobservable except as the wrong workload running.

Promoting Progressive Sync from beta to Stable is gated on the argoproj definition that stable features are tested and validated with various use cases, but the wide-eye view of progressive sync that would supply that validation is itself still an open request — the metrics answering how long a sync took to trigger, how long step X took, how many refreshes the ApplicationSet caused, and which Application a sync is waiting on do not exist yet. The promotion issue scopes remaining work by pointing at open enhancement and bug labels and never names this measurement dependency, so the maturity claim would have to be asserted rather than measured.
